[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The ECS service's VPC Lattice configuration uses the infrastructure IAM role, but the service does not wait for the VPC Lattice policy attachment. The existing dependency on the EBS policy attachment does not ensure this separate policy is attached before ECS configures the service.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The ECS service can be created before the infrastructure role's VPC Lattice managed policy is attached; add an explicit dependency so ECS does not use the role before it has the required VPC Lattice permissions.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The ECS service uses the infrastructure role for VPC Lattice, but it can be created before the VPC Lattice permissions are attached. Add an ordering dependency so ECS does not configure the service with a role that is not yet authorized for VPC Lattice.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_ecs_service.this uses the ECS infrastructure IAM role for VPC Lattice (vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn = local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn, i.e. aws_iam_role.infrastructure_iam_role), but its depends_on only waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy, not the VPC Lattice policy attachment. The AmazonECSInfrastructureRolePolicyForVpcLattice policy must be attached to the role before the service is created (and must outlive it), otherwise ECS may be unable to assume the role / perform Lattice actions, or the policy could be destroyed too early (DRAINING race). Add aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy to the service's depends_on. No clean attribute-based fix exists (there is no attribute on the service that references the attachment).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_ecs_service.this` passes `local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn` into `vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn`, but its `depends_on` only waits for `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy` (the EBS/volumes policy). The VPC Lattice managed policy attachment is never ordered before the service, so when `vpc_lattice_configurations` is set Terraform may call CreateService/UpdateService while the infrastructure role still lacks AmazonECSInfrastructureRolePolicyForVpcLattice, causing an AccessDenied failure. Add `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy` to the service's `depends_on`, mirroring the existing EBS policy entry.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`aws_ecs_service.this` sets `vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn = local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn`, so ECS will call VPC Lattice APIs with the infrastructure role at service-creation time. The module already guards the EBS variant (`aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy` is in `depends_on`) but omits `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy`, so service creation can race the policy attachment and fail with an authorization error. Add the VPC Lattice policy attachment to `depends_on`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`aws_ecs_service.this` passes the infrastructure role ARN (`local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn`) to `vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn`, but it only has an explicit `depends_on` on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy` and the role itself. When `vpc_lattice_configurations` is set, ECS uses the infrastructure role during service creation, so the `AmazonECSInfrastructureRolePolicyForVpcLattice` attachment must be in place first — otherwise service creation can fail with AccessDenied. The equivalent EBS attachment is already covered by `depends_on`; the VPC Lattice attachment is not.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The service passes `role_arn = local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn` into `vpc_lattice_configurations`, but only has a depends_on on the EBS infrastructure role policy attachment. When VPC Lattice configurations are used, the `AmazonECSInfrastructureRolePolicyForVpcLattice` attachment (`aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy`) must be attached (and propagated) before the service is created, otherwise ECS cannot assume the role with the required permissions. A bare `depends_on` is needed here since no attribute of the service can reference the attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
When `vpc_lattice_configurations` is set, the ECS service passes `role_arn` = the ECS infrastructure IAM role, and AWS uses that role to register/manage VPC Lattice target groups on the service's behalf. The module explicitly adds `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy` to both services' `depends_on` for exactly this reason (the analogous EBS infrastructure policy), but the parallel `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy` is not in either service's `depends_on` and is referenced by no other resource. If the service is created before that attachment exists, the infrastructure role has no `VPCLatticeServiceNetworkAccess` permissions yet, and ECS operations on the Lattice target groups can fail with AccessDenied. Since there is no attribute on the service that references the attachment (the role reference goes through the IAM role itself, not the attachment), a bare `depends_on` entry is the idiomatic fix.

When VPC Lattice is configured, this ECS service uses the infrastructure IAM role but does not wait for its VPC Lattice policy attachment. The service's current explicit dependencies cover the EBS policy attachment only.

The ECS service variant can be created before the infrastructure role's VPC Lattice managed policy is attached, even though it configures VPC Lattice; it should wait for the required permissions to be attached.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition uses the ECS infrastructure IAM role for VPC Lattice (vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn = local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn, i.e. aws_iam_role.infrastructure_iam_role), but its depends_on only waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy, not the VPC Lattice policy attachment. The AmazonECSInfrastructureRolePolicyForVpcLattice policy must be attached to the role before the service is created (and outlive it), otherwise ECS may fail to assume the role / perform Lattice actions, or the policy could be destroyed too early (DRAINING race). Add aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy to depends_on. No clean attribute-based fix exists.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition` also uses `local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn` for `vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn`, yet its `depends_on` waits only for `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy`. Nothing orders `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy` before the service, so a service with VPC Lattice configuration can be created before the infrastructure role has the required policy, failing with an authorization error. Add the VPC Lattice policy attachment to this resource's `depends_on` as well.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition` also passes `vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn = local.infrastructure_iam_role_arn` but only depends on the EBS policy attachment (via `depends_on`), not `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy`. Creating the service before the VPC Lattice policy is attached to the infrastructure role can fail. Add the VPC Lattice policy attachment to `depends_on`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition` passes the infrastructure role ARN to `vpc_lattice_configurations.role_arn` and volume configuration exactly like `aws_ecs_service.this`, but its `depends_on` only covers `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service` and `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy`. When `vpc_lattice_configurations` is set, the `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy` must be applied before the service is created so ECS can use the role for VPC Lattice operations.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
Same issue as `aws_ecs_service.this`: this variant of the service also passes the infrastructure IAM role ARN into `vpc_lattice_configurations` but only depends on the EBS policy attachment, not on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy`. The VPC Lattice policy must be attached and propagated before the service is created. A bare `depends_on` is needed here since no attribute of the service can reference the attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
Same issue as `aws_ecs_service.this`: `aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition` supports the `vpc_lattice_configurations` block, and when it is configured the service relies on the ECS infrastructure IAM role having the VPC Lattice policy attached. The resource's `depends_on` includes `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service` and `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_ebs_policy`, but omits `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy`, which exists solely to attach that permission to the infrastructure role and which nothing else in the graph depends on. Creation ordering is therefore unconstrained relative to that attachment, risking AccessDenied failures on Lattice-related ECS operations. A bare `depends_on` entry (matching the pattern already used for the EBS policy attachment) closes the gap; no data-reference alternative exists because the service only references the role ARN, not the attachment.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_ecs_task_definition.this uses aws_iam_role.tasks as task_role_arn, and its depends_on already waits for the task-role's external policy attachment (aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks) plus the execution-role attachments, but it does NOT wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal, which attaches the module-created policy (aws_iam_policy.tasks, granting ECS Exec / custom task-role statements) to the very same aws_iam_role.tasks. This asymmetry means tasks could start before the task role has its ECS Exec permissions, and the policy could be torn down before the task definition. Add aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal to the task definition's depends_on. No clean attribute-based fix exists (task_role_arn references the role, not the attachment).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`aws_ecs_task_definition.this` explicitly depends on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks`, `...task_exec` and `...task_exec_additional` so tasks can assume their roles with permissions already in place, but it does not depend on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal`, which attaches the module-created task policy (e.g. the ECS Exec `ssmmessages:*` statements) to the same task role. With `enable_execute_command`/`tasks_iam_role_statements` set, a service can start tasks before that attachment exists, causing task failures. Add `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal` to `depends_on`.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`aws_ecs_task_definition.this` has an explicit `depends_on` on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks`, `task_exec`, and `task_exec_additional` to ensure role permissions are propagated before tasks launch, but it omits `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal`, which attaches the policy containing the ECS Exec (`ssmmessages:*`) statements and any `tasks_iam_role_statements` to the task role. Tasks created from this definition (e.g., by `aws_ecs_service.this` or `aws_ecs_task_set.this`) may launch before that attachment propagates, breaking ECS Exec and task-role permissions.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The task definition waits on the `tasks`, `task_exec`, and `task_exec_additional` role policy attachments via depends_on, but omits `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal`, which attaches the internal tasks policy (including the ECS Exec `ssmmessages:*` permissions) to the tasks role. AWS IAM propagation means the task role may not yet have those permissions when tasks launched from this definition start, breaking ECS Exec. This mirrors the existing depends_on guards already present on this resource.
